%% Proof of the derivability equivalence from the derivation maps of
%% sec:p02-w02b-p02-010-translations.
\begin{annexitem}{annex:p02-w02b-p02-010-calculi-equivalence}{thm:p02-calculi-derivability-equivalence}{Derivability equivalence of the classical calculi}
\begin{proof}
Let \(\Gamma\) be a finite set of full-language formulas and \(\varphi\) a
full-language formula.  The first equivalence is
\cref{thm:prop-completeness} from left to right and
\cref{thm:prop-nd-soundness} from right to left.  By
\cref{thm:p02-w02b-p02-010-hilbert-equivalence}(1),
\(\Gamma\derives_{\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{CPL}}}\varphi\) holds iff
\(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf H}[\Gamma]\derives_{\mathsf H_{\mathsf{CPL}}}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf H}(\varphi)\), which is the third equivalence.
By \cref{thm:p02-w02b-p02-010-hilbert-equivalence}(2), with \(\Gamma\) read
as a multiset of multiplicity one, the sequent \(\Gamma\Rightarrow\varphi\)
is derivable in \(\mathsf{LK}_{\mathsf{CPL}}\) iff the same Hilbert
condition holds; combining the two gives the second equivalence.  The
corollary is proved in \cref{annex:p02-w02b-p02-010-hilbert-equivalence}
by explicit derivation maps and uses no semantic notion, so the semantic
leg enters only through the first equivalence.
\end{proof}
\end{annexitem}
